current_bottleneck: The missing object is a flexible stochastic transition density that preserves AR/state feedback. Fixed Gaussian/Student-t likelihoods improve coverage but are too rigid; flow-matching transitions preserve structure but do not provide calibrated density training; one-shot path laws and bottlenecks repeatedly lose local geometry.
last_result_summary: 624 synthesized the 609-623 evidence and selected a minimal conditional normalizing-flow transition likelihood. The proposed model keeps one shared IV-only/joint38 panel interface and causal AR rollout, but replaces Gaussian/Student-t increments with an exact RealNVP-style conditional density over empirical-score increments.
next_step_recommendation: Implement and run 625a: a joint38 conditional RealNVP transition likelihood in raw empirical-score state coordinates, with alternating affine coupling layers, exact NLL training, and the existing official IV bridge. Acceptance is improvement over the 5/11 Student-t/AR frontier without losing the structural passes.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
